calibration: NOT well calibrated, and in the opposite direction expected. Sample: 22 high-confidence, 23 medium-confidence, 30 low-confidence records. Records with >=1 finding: high 10/22 (45%), medium 6/23 (26%), low 10/30 (33%). High-confidence records had the HIGHEST flagged-issue rate of the three tiers, not the lowest. Critically, the single 'critical' severity finding in the entire sample (tw-tairx citing a different company's stock-ticker page as its source) is on a confidence:high record, and one of the six 'major' findings (us-altos-labs wrong HQ city) is also confidence:high. Several other high-confidence records had unreachable sources or citation/support mismatches (cn-jd-health, cn-united-family-healthcare, cn-hua-medicine, eu-neko-health, il-sol-gel-technologies, in-qure-ai). Low-confidence records did surface real issues (il-metabomed likely-defunct domain, us-materna-medical wrong FDA clearance year, eu-neuromod-devices FDA pathway overstatement) but not at a materially higher rate than high-confidence ones. Conclusion: the confidence field appears to reflect how much source material the researching agent found, not whether that material was correctly transcribed — it is not a reliable proxy for correctness and should not be used to deprioritize review of 'high' records.
notes: Sample of 75 company records drawn from data/all-companies.json (1,193 total), stratified across all 12 regions with quotas weighted toward confidence:low, plus forced inclusion of the 10 largest total_raised/valuation records (cn-jd-health $5.4B, us-altos-labs $3.0B, eu-recipharm $2.1B, cn-united-family-healthcare $1.44B, eu-oura $1.2B, us-lifestance-health $1.2B, us-resilience $1.0B, eu-neko-health $1.0B, us-cityblock-health $900M) and one record already self-flagged in its own verification_notes (anz-advancell). Work was parallelized across 5 sub-agents (15 records each), each independently loading WebFetch and fetching company websites + every sources[] URL. Zero companies in the sample were dead/non-existent, and zero were miscategorized funds/accelerators — the dataset's basic integrity (real, disjoint operating companies) held up well. Errors instead cluster in: (1) HQ city/location drift as companies relocate/redomicile post-round (anz-advancell Boston HQ, us-altos-labs Redwood City not 'Los Altos', kr-jlk Seoul vs Cheongju); (2) source-quote mismatches where the citation doesn't literally contain the claimed support text even though the underlying fact is often still true elsewhere on the same domain (cn-hua-medicine, cn-united-family-healthcare, eu-sensyne-health); (3) one outright wrong source URL (tw-tairx pointing to a different company's stock listing page); (4) specific numeric/date drift on regulatory claims (us-materna-medical FDA clearance year off by 2, verified against openFDA 510(k) database) and funding round-stage labels (eu-oura 'growth' vs actual 'Series E', us-cityblock-health 'series-c-plus' vs actual 'Series D'). [chunk1] Chunk overall is in good shape — no dead domains, no fund/accelerator miscategorized as an operating company, and every 'what it does' description matched the live website. The most interesting pattern is a cluster of minor sourcing-hygiene issues rather than factual errors: (1) two BetaKit citations (CareGuide, EmergConnect) point at live search-query URLs instead of stable article permalinks — the content still checks out today but the citation is fragile; (2) the Nicoya founding-date quote is real but lives on a different page than the cited URL; (3) Hua Medicine's regulatory (NMPA/2022) claim is true but not actually supported by its cited source — it required an independent fetch of huamedicine.com to confirm. AdvanCell is the one record where a field (country/hq_city = Australia/Sydney) is defensible today but sits on a real, current tension: the company's own PR now calls Boston its 'U.S. global headquarters' as of June 2026, which is exactly the kind of fast-moving fact a periodic audit should keep re-checking. No investor name in this chunk looked implausible for its round (Sanofi Ventures/SV Health/Morningside/Brandon Capital for AdvanCell's radiopharma Series D; Hillhouse for JD Health; Wesfarmers Health directly confirmed as SiSU Health's owner on SiSU's own site, which is actually stronger confirmation than the record's own cautious verification_notes suggested). | [chunk2] This chunk is notably clean: all 15 companies exist, match their descriptions, and are genuine operating companies (none turned out to be a VC fund/accelerator miscategorized as a portfolio company). Every website resolved to the right company except neko.health, which returned blank content from WebFetch on 3 attempts despite being clearly live and well-covered by press (likely a JS-heavy SPA or bot-blocking issue with the fetch tool, not a dead domain). The eu-neko-health record is the standout for source rigor in this chunk — 6 sources, all independently confirmed near-verbatim, spanning a 2023-2026 funding history (Series A $65M -> Series B $260M -> Series C $700M) that is internally consistent and matches TechCrunch reporting exactly, including a round dated 2026-07 that is plausible given today's date (2026-08-16).
